schema.user_judgment: 5-point: A++=A much better, A+=A slightly better, 0=about the same, B+=B slightly better, B++=B much better
schema.rules: predictions committed BEFORE user judgment; locked once user has rated

prediction.rationale: HWB C-corner reaches 100% of max sRGB chroma at h=240 (chroma 0.313 vs target 0.313). HPLuv reaches 58% (chroma 0.101 vs target 0.174). Both spaces hit pure white and pure black exactly.

Both hit 100% of max sRGB chroma AT THEIR RENDERED OKLrab HUE (HWB at 264°, OKHSL at 240°). Different absolute chromas (0.313 vs 0.164) because sRGB gamut is anisotropic — blue corner is more chromatic than OKLab-true-blue. Per the §13.1 definition, both pass Reach.
prediction.calibration_question: If you judge Reach by 'how saturated does the C corner LOOK' (absolute chroma), HWB is better. If you judge by 'does the C corner reach max possible at its rendered hue', they're tied. Which matches your eye? Either answer tells me which formula is right.

prediction.rationale: OKHSV is actually more linear than HWB on edges (W↔B 0.000 vs 0.034; B↔C 0.016 vs 0.034). Both have moderate W↔C non-linearity (0.136 vs 0.158). Net: OKHSV slightly better on edge linearity. If your earlier OKHSV-cramming complaint shows up here, my edge metric is missing it.

pairs.user_notes: HWB: same as before — B-W edge mildly dominated by white. OKHSV: black fully compacted into corner — much worse failure. My edge metric (B↔C dev 0.016) missed it entirely.

milestones.finding: OKLrab Lr is the right reference for adjacent-step ΔE measurements. Validated by black→blue ramp test: user prefers Lr-uniform spacing (cells visibly distinct in dark end, no JND-crushing) over L-uniform (dark stops compress below JND). Grayscale midpoint test gave a separate result (visual middle gray sits at OKLab L=0.5, not Lr=0.5) but that's about absolute middle-gray perception, not adjacent-step pacing — different question, doesn't affect ΔE measurements.
milestones.metric: Use OKLrab Lr ΔE for Smoothness and Distinctness measurements.

milestones.finding: User-validated metric for 'tiny corner' failure: count of stops in a 1-D scale whose OKLrab Lr falls below a darkness threshold (e.g., 0.20). Few stops below threshold = small dark zone = compacted black corner. Validated at h=240 normalized so each space's C corner = sRGB pure blue: user rated jzazbz most compacted and oklch least compacted; the metric ranks identically. Threshold-robust across 0.15, 0.20, 0.25, 0.30. Per-step ΔE / maxDev did not catch this — they measure pacing uniformity, not corner-influence size.
milestones.metric: For each 1-D scale, count stops in each corner's perceptual region: black corner |{Lr < 0.20}|; white corner |{Lr > 0.80}|; pure corner |{ΔE_to_corner < ~0.20}|. Few stops = tiny corner. Many stops = dominant corner. Penalty proportional to deviation from a target band per corner.

milestones.finding: Some spaces' interpolation between two corners drifts the OKLrab hue away from the corner's hue — e.g., HWB's W↔C (white-to-blue) path passes through purple before returning to blue. Visible artifact independent of compaction or pacing. User identified HWB and LCh(ab) as suffering this on W↔C at h=240; LCh peaks 32° off, HWB 21° off. OKLCH/OKHSL/OKHSV hold OKLrab hue constant by design (drift ≈ 0°).
milestones.metric: For each edge (or 1-D scale) ending at the C corner, compute OKLrab hue at every cell with chroma > some_min (e.g., 0.05). hueDrift = max over those cells of |hueCircular(cell) − hue(C_corner)|. Penalty above some threshold (e.g., 10°).

validation_data.edge: W↔C, hue normalized to sRGB blue (C target hue = 264.2°)
validation_data.user_observation: HWB and LCh(ab) go through purple on the way from white to blue.

milestones.finding: Aggregate v2 Smoothness (4 sub-metrics, quadratic-shortfall, equal weight) ranks the 6 UI spaces consistently with user's eye at the top and bottom. Tested at h=240 normalized so each space's C corner = sRGB pure blue, identity curves. Metric ranking: okhsv 92, oklch 81, okhsl 79, hwb 77, lchab 69, jzazbz 58. User-confirmed: best = okhsv, worst = jzazbz. Note: with custom user curves applied, HWB/OKLCH would likely pull ahead — calibration here was at identity curves only. Middle-ranking validation deferred.
milestones.metric_aggregation: Per 1-D scale: aggregateShortfall over [pacing, cornerInfluenceA, cornerInfluenceB, hueDrift?, chromaAdequacy?] — last two only when scale ends at C corner.
open_items: Validate at additional hues (currently sRGB-blue only)
Validate middle-rankings (3 of 4 middle spaces unranked)

milestones.finding: Some spaces' interpolation between W and C never builds chroma in the interior — the path stays low-chroma for most of its length, then jumps to the C corner's chroma at the end. OKHSL is the canonical example: at the W↔C midpoint, chroma is only 26% of the C-corner's chroma (linear-ideal would be 50%). User identified this as 'extremely desaturated grays' on the way to blue.
milestones.metric: For each edge starting at W or B and ending at C, compute chroma at the midpoint stop / chroma at the C-corner stop. Linear-ideal = 0.5. Significantly less than 0.5 indicates 'chroma collapse' (path keeps colors muted, then jumps).

validation_data.edge: W↔C, hue normalized to sRGB blue
validation_data.user_observation: OKHSL goes through extremely desaturated grays before arriving at blue.
